record.paper_title: Chebyshev Sets, Klee Sets, and Chebyshev Centers with respect to Bregman Distances: Recent Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Characterizing right D-Chebyshev sets for negative entropy
record.original_question: Let X = R^n_{++} be the strictly positive orthant, and let f be the negative entropy Legendre function whose Bregman distance is the Kullback-Leibler divergence on positive vectors. A subset C of X is right D-Chebyshev when every x in X has a unique y in C minimizing D(x, y). Closed convex subsets are known to be right D-Chebyshev in this setting, and there also exist nonconvex right D-Chebyshev subsets. Can one characterize exactly which subsets of the strictly positive orthant are right D-Chebyshev for this negative-entropy Bregman distance?

evidence.quote: Fact 3.4 (See [6, Lemma 3.5].) Suppose that f is the negative entropy (see Example 1.1(ii)) and that C is convex. Then C is ->D-Chebyshev.

Combining Example 3.3 and Fact 3.4, we deduce that - when working with the negative entropy - if C is convex, then C is ->D-Chebyshev but not vice versa. Is it possible to describe the ->D-Chebyshev sets in this setting?

Problem 4. Is it possible to characterize the class of ->D-Chebyshev subsets of the strictly positive orthant when f is the negative entropy? Fact 3.4 and Example 3.3 imply that this class contains not only all closed convex but also some nonconvex subsets.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X = \mathbb{R}^n_{++} = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^n : x_i > 0 \text{ for all } i\}$ denote the strictly positive orthant. Define the negative entropy function $f: \mathbb{R}^n_{++} \to \mathbb{R}$ by
$$f(x) = \sum_{i=1}^n x_i \log x_i - \sum_{i=1}^n x_i,$$
(with the convention $0 \log 0 = 0$ for boundary considerations). The associated Bregman distance is the (generalized) Kullback–Leibler divergence
$$D(x,y) = f(x) - f(y) - \langle \nabla f(y), x - y \rangle = \sum_{i=1}^n \left( x_i \log \frac{x_i}{y_i} - x_i + y_i \right), \qquad x,y \in \mathbb{R}^n_{++}.$$

A subset $C \subseteq X$ is called right D-Chebyshev if for every $x \in X$ there exists a unique $y \in C$ that minimizes $D(x, \cdot)$ over $C$. It is known that every nonempty closed convex subset of $X$ is right D-Chebyshev, and that there exist nonconvex subsets of $X$ which are also right D-Chebyshev.

Problem: Give an intrinsic characterization of the class of right D-Chebyshev subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n_{++}$ with respect to this Kullback–Leibler Bregman distance.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any work providing a complete characterization of the right D-Chebyshev subsets of the positive orthant for the Kullback–Leibler (negative-entropy) Bregman distance. Related literature treats existence/uniqueness of Bregman projections for convex sets and partial results, but no characterization has been located, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Categories of Brègman operations and epistemic (co)monads
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses left and right D_Ψ-Chebyshev sets and projections in Bregman settings, treating them as objects of ongoing study rather than fully characterized.
status_evidence.claim: The literature on right D-Chebyshev sets still treats their characterization as an open structural question.
